source_id.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Which record in the source tool is this? The record's own key in the tool it came from, so any node can be traced back to its system of record. Distinct from SDEM `id`, which may be the same value.

owner.description: the actor or role accountable for it

x-sdem-source.standard: ArchiMate 3.2 concept (confirmed via the Archi oracle; specification text login-gated)
x-sdem-source.locator: assignment (active structure assigned to behaviour or object)

owner.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Who is accountable for this? Accountability is the most-asked design question. No public standard defines an "owner" field: Dublin Core's rightsHolder is about rights, not accountability. Built on ArchiMate's assignment of an actor or role.

access_classification.description: how sensitive it is and who may see it

access_classification.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Who may see this? How sensitive is it? Dublin Core defines the field (access or security status); the four values are SDEM's common banking scale, not a standard.

x-sdem-source.standard: ArchiMate 3.2 (relationship)

criticality.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Which critical processes depend on this platform or application? The single most useful field for impact analysis. No open standard defines it; business-continuity standards (ISO 22301) are paid.

x-sdem-source.standard: SDEM-defined (no open standard)

frequency.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: How often does it run? What is the blast radius of an outage? How often the process runs; informs outage impact.

automation_level.x-sdem-reasoning: Answers: Where is manual effort? What is a candidate for automation? Degree of automation; no standard scale.

x-sdem-entity.reasoning: SDEM extension of Business Process: ArchiMate decomposes a process into sub-processes (composition) rather than a separate activity element; SDEM names the lowest level an activity, the level at which a step invokes one BIAN operation.
